paragraphs: Rav Yechiel. (The biblical name parallel is Yechiel son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, II Chronicles 21:2; this is not an identification.) Hyman describes him as a great man in the time of Rav Yehuda, Rav Chisda and R' Nachman. In Moed Katan 10a [supplied: כמ״ק י:], where they asked, What is "mekhavshin"? Rav Yehuda said, chiseling a millstone; and Rav Yechiel said, a bat eina [central opening of a millstone]. And in Eruvin 31b: Rav Chisda said, [it works if the sender] stands and watches; [and the objection,] perhaps he did not receive it from him? Rav Yechiel said, there is a presumption that an agent carries out his mission. R' Nachman said, in a matter of Torah law there is no such presumption.
And he is likewise mentioned in Eruvin 12a: Rav Achili, and some say Rav Yechiel, said, up to four; and there, 28b:

Rav Chelkiah son of Tuviah said, one may establish an eruv with kalya greens; and how much? Rav Yechiel said, a handful. And there, 76a, he said: An overturned [bowl; supplied כפל] reduces [the height].
And in Beitzah 14b: Rav Yechiel taught, provided that he not make it in a row; and in Yoma 46a: Rabbah bar Yonatan said in the name of Rabbi Yechiel, gruel is good for a sick person.

notes.text: Kalya is a vegetable in the checked Eruvin28b witness, and its measure is a handful. The later fragment prints כפל and remains unclear. The gruel statement’s printed Yoma46a locator was not matched in that digital witness.
The milling term בת עינא is retained here as bat eina; its precise technical sense remains unresolved in this review.

Every explicit full Rav title in the heading and supplied quotations is retained, including Rav Yehuda, Rav Chisda, Rav Yechiel, Rav Achili and Rav Chelkiah; Tuviah and Rabbah bar Yonatan receive no transferred title. The two abbreviated Nachman titles are R', with Nachman retained as the inherited contextual expansion. The old Eruvin31b note quotes full Rav Nachman, but that quote has not been re-read as a whole selected scalar here and does not transfer a full title to the separate generation statement. The Yoma quotation alone uses Rabbi Yechiel on exact local support from the whole saved Davidson Yoma47a scalar; it does not resolve whether every Yechiel here is the same person. Hyman's great-man and contemporary-generation statement remains his claim. The biblical Yechiel son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, II Chronicles21:2, remains a name parallel, not an identification. The supplied locators remain Moed Katan10b (כמ״ק י:), Eruvin76a (עו.) and Yoma46a (מו.) in the translation. The whole saved Davidson matches are Moed Katan10a, Eruvin77a and Yoma47a respectively; neither locators nor Hebrew letters are silently repaired, and the digital matches do not establish a printing or correction history. Bat eina stays untranslated: the Arukh/Jastrow central-hole gloss and Rashi wall-height gloss were only search snippets, not whole lexical or commentary witnesses read here. The whole Eruvin28b scalar supports kalya greens and a handful, rather than the older sound/handspan proposal; its extra rhetorical objection is absent from Hyman's compressed quotation and is not imported. The whole Eruvin77a scalar reads כפה ספל ממעט, an overturned bowl reduces; supplied כפל remains visible and unresolved as source text. The Yoma47a scalar names Rabbah bar Yonatan reporting Rabbi Yechiel and supports gruel is good for a sick person; its preceding material and alternative explanations are not imported. All four selected scalars were read whole, with raw hash, selectors and actual edition metadata checked. Eruvin12a's alternative Achili/Yechiel, up to four, and the transition to28b remain; Beitzah14b's row prohibition remains. Earlier bounded nonmatches at10b/76a/46a/39a remain historical observations, not global absence or retroactive PASS. All three old mixed notes, both current notes, all older English and original note responses remain exact. This is one additive qualification; p001, p003 and p004 source holds all remain.

The consulted scan of Hyman II, p. 756, prints Moed Katan י., 10a, beside the supplied transcription’s י:, 10b. The English follows the printed 10a and records the supplied alternative. Rashi on Moed Katan 10a explicitly explains bat eina as the hole made in the middle of a millstone into which the grain falls; the bracketed English gloss follows this whole consulted comment. This is a newly read Rashi witness, not a fresh collation of the Arukh or Jastrow. The same Hyman print still gives Eruvin 76a and Yoma 46a: the modern matches at 77a and 47a remain comparisons, not corrections established from the print. Printed כפל also remains beside the modern ספל, “bowl.” The whole Eruvin 31b passage confirms the agency exchange and Nahman’s Torah-law qualification; it does not transfer titles to every other occurrence. Eruvin 12a preserves Achlai or Yechiel and “up to four”; Beitzah 14b gives the row or convoy restriction without adding its omitted discussion. The whole Yoma 47a passage locally names Rabbi Yechiel in the gruel saying. The biblical name remains a parallel, and the contemporary-generation description is Hyman’s. The earlier technical and locator notes remain verbatim, followed by this additional comparison.
